articles.title: Radiographic criteria and results of bone graft incorporation in bony increased-offset reverse shoulder arthroplasty: A systematic review.
articles.authors: De Rosa A, Cardinale ME, Di Fabio S, Paciotti M, Franceschetti E, Ciuffreda M, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review of structural bone grafting in reverse shoulder arthroplasty
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse shoulder arthroplasty with structural glenoid bone grafting
articles.outcomes: Radiographic graft incorporation, graft resorption, mechanical failure, scapular notching
articles.take_home: Radiographic signs of graft resorption were seen in 6.3% of shoulders, but only 1.9% had true mechanical failure, suggesting that most radiographic changes represent normal biological remodeling rather than serious problems. However, there is currently no standardised way to evaluate bone grafts after this surgery, making it difficult to interpret X-ray findings.

articles.title: Development of Convolutional Neural Networks for Classification and Characterisation of Proximal Humerus Fractures on Computed Tomography.
articles.authors: Mennes SRJ, Spek RWA, Zhang X, Qi X, Liao Z, Trouwborst NM, et al.
articles.study_type: Machine learning model development and validation study
articles.population: Patients with proximal humerus fractures on CT scans
articles.sample_size: 581 Australian patients (training) and 122 Dutch patients (external validation)
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of artificial intelligence classification of fracture type and characterisation of greater tuberosity displacement, varus malalignment, shaft translation and articular involvement compared to surgeon assessment
articles.take_home: A machine learning model accurately identified greater tuberosity displacement and varus malalignment in shoulder fractures on CT scans, performing as well as or better than experienced surgeons in some areas. However, the model needs improvement for identifying certain types of bone displacement and joint surface involvement before it can be used in clinical practice.

articles.title: Effect of Combined Tendon Remnant Preservation and Bone Marrow Stimulation on Rotator Cuff Healing: A Propensity Score-Matched Study.
articles.authors: Scaini A, Maggini E, Daffara V, Guizzi A, Bergomi A, Milano G
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort comparison with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing arthroscopic rotator cuff repair
articles.outcomes: American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score, Quick-DASH scale, Western Ontario Rotator Cuff Index, and tendon healing on MRI at six months
articles.take_home: Preserving the rotator cuff tendon remnant combined with small bone vents improved tendon healing rates (81% versus 54%), although both surgical approaches led to similar improvements in patient-reported shoulder function at follow-up.

articles.title: Dynamic analysis of nerves around the elbow using MRI-derived 3-D modeling.
articles.authors: Saeki T, Murakami Y, Iwase H, Yamamoto M
articles.study_type: Basic science study using MRI imaging and 3D modelling
articles.population: Healthy volunteers
articles.outcomes: Distance between nerves and bony landmarks at different elbow angles; reliability of 3D nerve model creation; optimal elbow positions for surgical portals
articles.take_home: Researchers successfully created 3D models of nerves around the elbow from MRI scans and found that when the elbow bends, the nerve at the outer side moves further away from the bone landmark surgeons use. This information could help surgeons position the elbow safely during arthroscopic surgery to avoid damaging nerves.

articles.title: Multiplanar CT-based characterization of offset and positional change in reverse shoulder arthroplasty and validation of radiographic metrics.
articles.authors: Vervaecke AJ, Verborgt O, Werthel JD
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Correlation between radiographic metrics (LSA, DSA, LI, DI) and CT-based measurements of implant position and positional change
articles.take_home: After reverse shoulder replacement, standard X-ray measurements do not accurately reflect where the implant actually sits or how much it has moved compared to before surgery, based on detailed CT scans. The implant's centre of rotation shifts inward and downward, but current X-ray angles and ratios do not reliably capture these changes.

articles.title: Antibiotic Elution from PMMA Over 60 Days: an in vitro Study of 21 antibiotic combinations against C. acnes and Coagulase Negative Staph. (CNS).
articles.authors: DiPaola MJ, Carinha M, Masood U, Crane J
articles.population: Four bacterial strains from shoulder infections: two coagulase-negative staph strains and two C. acnes strains
articles.sample_size: 21 different antibiotic combinations tested in triplicate
articles.outcomes: Antibiotic elution from PMMA beads over 60 days measured by bacterial growth suppression in vitro
articles.take_home: Several antibiotic combinations successfully suppressed bacterial growth for the full 60 days when mixed with bone cement, with rifampin alone or combined with vancomycin or doxycycline being most effective. Vancomycin with doxycycline also showed strong suppression against all tested bacteria.

articles.title: Evaluation of Spin Bias in Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Comparing Bankart Repair with Remplissage Versus the Latarjet Procedure.
articles.authors: Olaonipekun E, Abdou M, Ade-Conde AM, McCay S, Kruse C, Bouchard M, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
articles.population: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses comparing Bankart repair with remplissage versus Latarjet procedure for anterior shoulder instability
articles.sample_size: 13 systematic reviews (7 with meta-analyses); median 16 primary studies and 778 shoulders per review
articles.outcomes: Prevalence of spin bias (misrepresentation or overinterpretation) in abstract reporting; methodological quality assessed by AMSTAR-2
articles.take_home: Spin bias was found in 12 of 13 systematic review abstracts (92%), most commonly overstating benefits or claiming equivalence despite weak evidence. Most reviews had critically low or low methodological quality, so clinicians should be cautious when using these reviews to decide between shoulder surgery options.

articles.title: Early EMG-based Low Supraspinatus Activity Exercises After Arthroscopic Repair of Medium-Sized Rotator Cuff Tears: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Kus G, Celik D, Atalar AC
articles.population: Patients who underwent arthroscopic repair of full-thickness, medium-sized rotator cuff tears
articles.outcomes: Pain, shoulder range of motion, muscle strength, shoulder function, quality of life, and patient satisfaction measured over 12 months
articles.take_home: Starting gentle exercises that place minimal stress on the repaired rotator cuff one week after surgery reduced pain and discomfort in the short term compared to keeping the arm immobilised for four weeks. At 12 months, there were no differences between the two groups in movement, strength, function, or overall satisfaction.

articles.title: Higher body weight and current smoking are associated with lower concentrations of perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis in the synovial fluid of the shoulder joint.
articles.authors: Ubl ST, Arnold LM, Pfeiffer TR, Krombholz S, Imach S, Kappel P, et al.
articles.population: Adults undergoing arthroscopic or open shoulder surgery
articles.outcomes: Unbound cefazolin concentration in shoulder synovial fluid; factors affecting antibiotic levels
articles.take_home: Patients with higher body weight and those who currently smoke had lower levels of antibiotic in their shoulder joint fluid after receiving a standard 2 gram dose of cefazolin before surgery. The researchers suggest that antibiotic doses may need adjusting based on individual patient characteristics.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes Following Arthroscopic Pectoralis Minor Release.
articles.authors: Reihl AM, McBroom TJ, Wiley N, Vasquez D, Omurzakov A, Lohre R, et al.
articles.population: Patients with pectoralis minor syndrome and neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome
articles.sample_size: 273 patients (164 also received brachial plexus neurolysis)
articles.outcomes: Significant improvements in shoulder pain, function, and arm disability scores; improved shoulder forward elevation; 4.4% complication rate
articles.take_home: Arthroscopic pectoralis minor release is safe and effective for treating pectoralis minor syndrome and associated nerve symptoms, with most patients experiencing meaningful improvements in pain and shoulder function. Unusual muscle anatomy was not more common in these patients, suggesting overactive muscle rather than structural abnormality is usually the problem.

articles.title: Triceps-sparing approach results in better elbow function compared to triceps-detaching approach in total elbow arthroplasty: A multicenter prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Meijering D, Boerboom AL, Gerritsma CLE, The B, van den Bekerom MPJ, van der Pluijm M, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total elbow arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Fixed flexion deformity, range of motion, triceps strength, self-reported function, component positioning, complications
articles.take_home: Patients who had surgery that preserved their triceps tendon had better elbow straightening and movement than those whose triceps was detached, though both groups reported similar satisfaction and had comparable complication rates around 44%.

articles.title: Computerized Branching Logic Systems Significantly Improve the Accuracy of ASES Scores for Patients with Bilateral Shoulder Pain Undergoing Shoulder Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Bozoghlian M, Galvin J, Rojas E, Patterson BM
articles.study_type: Retrospective comparative study of outcome measurement methodology
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary shoulder arthroplasty with minimum 1-year follow-up, including those who developed contralateral shoulder pain
articles.sample_size: 188 patients (27 pre-branching logic with bilateral pain, 29 post-branching logic with bilateral pain, 132 pre-branching logic without contralateral pain)
articles.outcomes: ASES scores, VAS pain scores and range of motion at 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months and 1 year postoperatively
articles.take_home: A computerised branching logic system improved the accuracy of ASES shoulder function scores in patients with bilateral shoulder pain by allowing clearer distinction between pain from the operated shoulder and the new contralateral shoulder. Without this system, ASES scores incorrectly appeared to worsen over time due to unclear reporting of which shoulder caused the pain.

articles.title: In Silico Biomechanical Performance of Inlay vs. Onlay Glenoid Implants in Total Shoulder Arthroplasty: A Finite Element Study.
articles.authors: Chapai S, Dhar U, Papp DF, Tsai CT, Miniaci A
articles.population: Virtual healthy shoulder model based on CT scan
articles.outcomes: Contact forces and stresses at the glenoid component and surrounding bone in inlay versus onlay glenoid designs
articles.take_home: Computer modelling suggests that inlay glenoid implants distribute loads more evenly with surrounding bone and experience lower stresses than onlay implants, which may explain why inlay implants tend to last longer in clinical practice.

articles.title: Quantitative Assessment of Ulnohumeral Instability After K-NOW Unlinked Total Elbow Arthroplasty Using the Helical Axis: A Pilot Study.
articles.authors: Sugiura Y, Iwamoto T, Matsumoto Y, Kiyota Y, Suzuki T, Nagura T, et al.
articles.study_type: Pilot study comparing elbow kinematics using helical axis analysis
articles.population: Healthy volunteers and patients who had unlinked total elbow arthroplasty (K-NOW prosthesis)
articles.sample_size: 10 elbows from 5 healthy volunteers and 5 elbows from 4 patients after surgery
articles.outcomes: Translational displacement along the helical axis and stability of elbow motion during flexion-extension under different conditions
articles.take_home: Elbows that have had unlinked total elbow replacement show more side-to-side movement (laxity) than healthy elbows, particularly when the forearm is rotated. A small weight applied during testing did not appear to increase instability further.

articles.title: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and complications following primary total shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Ninness H, Rogalski BL, Ponce B, Eichinger JK, Friedman RJ
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Transfusion rates at 90 days and 1 year, revision surgery rates and mechanical failure at 5 years
articles.take_home: Although patients taking SSRIs had slightly higher transfusion and revision rates than those not taking SSRIs, these differences were not caused by the SSRIs themselves when other factors were accounted for. SSRIs appear to be safe to continue before shoulder replacement surgery.

articles.title: Preoperative acromiohumeral distance does not influence clinical outcomes after middle trapezius tendon transfer for irreparable supraspinatus tears.
articles.authors: Baek CH, Kim BT, Kim JG, Lim C, Kim SJ
articles.population: Patients with irreparable supraspinatus tears treated with middle trapezius tendon transfer
articles.outcomes: Pain (VAS), function (ASES and Constant scores), range of motion, muscle strength, and acromiohumeral distance
articles.take_home: Middle trapezius tendon transfer significantly improved pain and shoulder function in patients with irreparable supraspinatus tears, and the results were similar regardless of how much the shoulder joint had narrowed before surgery.

articles.title: Non-spherical head designs in total shoulder arthroplasty: A systematic review of clinical and biomechanical data.
articles.authors: Daher M, Haj Shehadeh T, Parmar T, Miniaci A, Abboud JA, Kassam HF
articles.study_type: Systematic review of biomechanical and clinical studies
articles.population: Patients undergoing total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Glenohumeral kinematics, range of motion, anatomic replication, contact mechanics, coverage, radiographic outcomes, patient-reported outcome measures, and implant-related complications
articles.take_home: Non-spherical humeral head designs in shoulder replacement showed better coverage and improved or similar outcomes compared to standard spherical designs in laboratory and clinical studies, though the evidence was sometimes contradictory. One clinical study found better range of motion with non-spherical designs.

articles.title: Validity and robustness of an AI-based tool for the assessment of shoulder joint range of motion in patients with shoulder pathologies.
articles.authors: Willi R, Schulz E, Rode D, Schneller T, Moroder P, Audige L, et al.
articles.population: Patients with unilateral shoulder conditions (rotator cuff lesions, instability or ligament rupture)
articles.outcomes: Range of motion measurements for shoulder flexion, abduction, internal rotation and other movements, compared between AI tool (Maia), motion capture system and visual estimation
articles.take_home: An AI video analysis tool called Maia measured shoulder movement with similar accuracy to the gold-standard motion capture system and was more accurate than visual estimation by a surgeon. The tool could be useful for monitoring patients over time or in remote consultations, though it was less reliable for measuring internal rotation movements.

articles.title: Association between pain intensity, range of motion, disability, and mental health-related quality of life variables in frozen shoulder: A cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Brindisino F, Feller D, Andriesse A, Venturin D, Poser A
articles.population: Adults with frozen shoulder at their first physiotherapy consultation
articles.outcomes: Pain intensity, disability, range of motion (flexion, abduction, external rotation), and mental health-related quality of life
articles.take_home: Pain was the main factor driving disability in frozen shoulder, and forward arm movement was most affected by pain. The study did not find clear links between pain and mental health-related quality of life at the start of treatment.

articles.title: Seasonal timing of surgery does not affect clinical outcomes in reverse total shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Erickson BJ, Denard PJ, Gobezie R, Lederman E, Sears B, Werner BC
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Patient reported outcomes, range of motion, complications and strength at 2 years follow up
articles.take_home: The season in which patients have reverse shoulder replacement surgery does not meaningfully affect their recovery or results at 2 years. Patients can proceed with surgery at any time of year without concern about timing affecting their outcome.
